identity.name: last30days
identity.one_liner: Open-source agent skill for researching what people said about any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, GitHub, and the web in the last 30 days.
identity.short_description: last30days is an open-source AI agent skill that searches recent public signals across social, developer, prediction-market, and web sources, then synthesizes a grounded brief. It is designed for recency-sensitive research where upvotes, likes, comments, transcripts, odds, commits, and discussions matter more than static search results.

positioning.why_it_matters: Most agent research fails when the question depends on what changed this month. last30days gives agents a reusable workflow for recent, multi-source, engagement-weighted research instead of relying only on generic web search.
best_for: Researchers who need recent community signal across multiple platforms
AI builders tracking fast-moving tools, prompts, repositories, and product sentiment
Operators preparing for meetings, launches, sales calls, or market scans with fresh context
not_for: Users who only need evergreen facts from official documentation
Teams that cannot use public social or web signals in their research workflow
Projects that require a fully offline research process

core_strengths.title: Multi-source recent research
core_strengths.description: last30days searches across Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, and the web depending on available configuration.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Fast-moving topics rarely live in one source. Multi-source coverage helps agents find what communities, markets, and developers are saying now.

core_strengths.title: Engagement-weighted signal
core_strengths.description: The skill emphasizes upvotes, likes, comments, transcripts, prediction-market odds, and repository activity as signals.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Engagement is imperfect, but it gives agents a useful way to prioritize what real people recently reacted to.

core_strengths.title: Skill-native install path
core_strengths.description: The repository supports Claude plugin installation and Agent Skills hosts through `npx skills add mvanhorn/last30days-skill -g`.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: A skill-native workflow makes recent research reusable across coding agents and agent hosts instead of living as a one-off prompt.

seo_article.intro: last30days is an open-source agent skill for researching what people have said about a topic over the last 30 days.
seo_article.what_it_is: It is a reusable skill that searches recent public sources such as Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, and the web, then synthesizes a grounded brief.
seo_article.why_it_matters: Recency-sensitive research is hard for agents because the useful signals are scattered across walled gardens and fast-moving communities. last30days packages that workflow into a skill.
seo_article.how_it_works: Install the skill, ask for a topic with `/last30days`, and review the synthesized brief. Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, and GitHub are designed to work immediately; additional sources can be unlocked with optional keys or auth.

use_cases.title: AI tool research
use_cases.description: Track recent reactions, repository movement, and community pain points around AI tools and frameworks.

use_cases.title: Market and product discovery
use_cases.description: Use social and prediction-market signals to understand what people are discussing before a launch or investment of time.

use_cases.title: People and company briefs
use_cases.description: Prepare for meetings with recent public context instead of relying on stale profile pages.

alternatives.title: Use ordinary web search for canonical facts
alternatives.summary: For stable documentation or evergreen facts, regular web search is simpler. For recent community signal, last30days is more targeted.

faq.question: Is last30days open source?
faq.answer: Yes. The GitHub repository is listed under the MIT license.

faq.question: Does last30days require API keys?
faq.answer: The README says Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, and GitHub work immediately. Optional keys or auth can unlock sources such as X, YouTube, TikTok, and more.

faq.question: Who should evaluate last30days?
faq.answer: Anyone doing recency-sensitive research for products, sales, markets, open-source projects, or fast-moving AI topics should evaluate it.
